author: Mark Atwood
text:
Public-API design choice independent of .18 (inner repr) but interlocking with .20 (redundant conversion API) and .4 (from_bytes rename, just landed). Defer to human.

CURRENT SHAPE (post bd:JMAP-sf5h.4)
- pub fn from_raw_digest(b: &[u8; 32]) -> Self — named constructor, infallible.
- No From<[u8; 32]> or From<&[u8; 32]> impl.

OPTIONS

(a) Drop from_raw_digest, add impl From<&[u8; 32]> for Sha256 (and optionally From<[u8; 32]>).
    - Callers write Sha256::from(&digest_bytes) or digest_bytes.into() — both self-documenting.
    - Matches RustCrypto Output<T>: From<GenericArray<u8, N>>.
    - Loses the descriptive name from_raw_digest that bd:JMAP-sf5h.4 just chose to disambiguate from sha2::Sha256::digest (the 'compute hash of bytes' convention).
    - Documentation can move into the From impl's rustdoc.

(b) Keep from_raw_digest, ADD impl From<&[u8; 32]>. Both paths exposed.
    - Maximizes ergonomics: descriptive name AND .into() works.
    - Adds redundant API surface — workspace canonical-templates rule says one-way-to-do-it.

(c) Keep from_raw_digest only. Status quo.
    - Defends the bd:JMAP-sf5h.4 rename win (named constructor = unambiguous direction).
    - Diverges from RustCrypto convention and from the wider Rust ecosystem 'infallible = From' idiom.

RECOMMENDATION: (a). The descriptive name was important when from_bytes read as 'hash these bytes'; once you write From<&[u8; 32]>::from at the call site, the input type ([u8; 32]) already disambiguates (no one calls hash-this-data with a 32-byte array). The rename-then-collapse-to-From sequence is forward-compatible — both edits land before publish, callers see only the final shape.

CASCADE IF (a) ACCEPTED: delete from_raw_digest, add impl From<&[u8; 32]>. Update tests, README, PLAN.md. Note: this composes with .20 — if (a) here AND .20 picks 'keep From<Sha256> for String, drop into_inner', then Sha256's conversion API becomes purely trait-based, no named constructors except from_hex (which is fallible and must be a named fn).

CASCADE IF (c) ACCEPTED: close .19 as 'declined-keep-named-constructor', noting the bd:JMAP-sf5h.4 rename rationale takes precedence over the From-impl idiom.
